facts.statement: The holotype specimen for Chuandongocoelurus primitivus is a thighbone catalogued as CCG 20010.
facts.quote: The holotype, a thighbone, is part of specimen CCG 20010.

facts.statement: The holotype thighbone of Chuandongocoelurus primitivus measures 201 millimetres in length.
facts.quote: The holotype thighbone has a length of 201 millimetres.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen had unfused neurocentral sutures, indicating the animal was immature when it died.
facts.quote: The specimen has unfused neurocentral sutures in its vertebrae, meaning that the animal was immature at the time of death.

facts.statement: In 2012, researchers concluded that the two specimens originally assigned to Chuandongocoelurus represent different taxa that are likely not closely related.
facts.quote: In 2012, it was concluded that both specimens represent different taxa, probably not even closely related.

facts.statement: Chuandongocoelurus lived during the Bathonian or Callovian stages of the Middle Jurassic, based on fossils found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: The formation in which it was discovered was the Lower Shaximiao Formation, meaning Chuandongocoelurus dates to the Bathonian or Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: The estimated total length of the Chuandongocoelurus holotype is 2.4 metres.
facts.quote: El holotipo tiene una longitud estimada de 2,4 metros.

facts.statement: Based on a femur length of 201 millimetres, the estimated body weight of Chuandongocoelurus ranges from 12 to 21.8 kilograms depending on the estimation method.
facts.quote: El fémur tiene 201 milímetros de longitud, de lo que se deriva un peso corporal de 21,8 kilogramos, una estimación de Michael Mortimer desde 2001 llegó a 12 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The tibia of the Chuandongocoelurus holotype measures 231 millimetres in length.
facts.quote: La tibia tiene una longitud de 231 milímetros.

facts.statement: Research by Roger Benson and colleagues suggests Chuandongocoelurus is the sister taxon of Monolophosaurus, forming a clade that may belong to Megalosauroidea or lie outside it within Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Roger Benson (2008, 2010) and Benson et al. (2010) found it to be the sister taxon of Monolophosaurus, together forming a clade belonging either to Megalosauroidea or outside of Megalosauroidea in the Tetanurae.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Matthew Carrano and colleagues placed Chuandongocoelurus outside the Megalosauroidea group.
facts.quote: In 2012, Matthew Carrano et al. found Chuandongocoelurus outside of the Megalosauroidea.

facts.statement: Chuandongocoelurus lived approximately 165 to 161 million years ago during the Bathonian and Callovian stages of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados período Jurásico, en el Bathoniense y Calloviense, hace aproximadamente entre 165 y 161 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: He Xinlu described Chuandongocoelurus in 1984 from remains found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation (part of the Dashanpu Formation), initially classifying it as a coelurosaurian.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por el palentologo chino He en 1984 a partir de restos descubiertos en la Formación Bajo Shaximiao, parte de la Formación Dashanpu, considerándolo como un coelurosaurio.

facts.statement: Distinctive anatomical features of Chuandongocoelurus include the base of the ilion being half the diameter of the hip joint, an accessory trochanter on the femur, and a tibial joint interior that is significantly enlarged.
facts.quote: Se han establecido algunas características distintivas, la base de la hoja frontal del ilion es la mitad del diámetro de la articulación de la cadera, hay un trocánter accesorio en el muslo para el trocánter menor, el interior de los huesos de la articulación inferior de la tibia es, con mucho, el más grande.

facts.statement: Chuandongocoelurus was originally classified within Coeluridae, a group at the time used as a catch-all for almost all small theropods.
facts.quote: Originalmente se colocó a Chuandongocoelurus en Coeluridae, en ese momento un taxón que incluía a casi todos los terópodos pequeños.

facts.statement: In 1990, David Bruce Norman considered Chuandongocoelurus to be an indeterminate theropod.
facts.quote: David Bruce Norman en 1990 lo consideraba un terópodo indeterminado.

rejected.quote: Chuandongocoelurus is a genus of carnivorous tetanuran theropod dinosaur from the Jurassic of China.
